title: Last Train, Softly
intent: A self-contained late-night noir jazz quartet for relaxation, maintaining gentle forward motion through understated swing and short motif exchanges.

tempo.feel: Gentle medium-slow swing with discreet walking bass, softened ride texture, and spacious phrasing.

tonality.mode: Lyrical major-minor interchange with chromatic mediant color

instrumentation.name: Hollow-body guitar
instrumentation.role: Introduces and restates the four-note motif with quiet chordal support.
instrumentation.timbre: Warm, woody, lightly amplified, clean fingerstyle articulation.

instrumentation.name: Alto saxophone
instrumentation.role: Reshapes the guitar motif in longer answering phrases; no extended solo.
instrumentation.timbre: Breathy, mellow, intimate, with restrained vibrato.

instrumentation.name: Upright bass
instrumentation.role: Provides a discreet walking foundation and briefly comes forward in the middle.
instrumentation.timbre: Round, woody, soft attack, lightly resonant.

instrumentation.name: Brush kit
instrumentation.role: Maintains understated swing and supports transitions.
instrumentation.timbre: Feathered snare brushes, softened ride, minimal cymbal brightness.

structure.direction: Hollow-body guitar alone presents a simple four-note cell in spacious voicings; bass and faint brushes enter gradually.
The quartet settles into gentle medium-slow swing. Guitar states the motif while bass walks discreetly and brushes remain soft.
Alto saxophone reshapes the motif in longer phrases; guitar answers with compact figures. Use lyrical major-minor interchange, secondary dominants, and brief chromatic mediant turns.
Thin the texture so upright bass briefly takes the foreground, with sparse guitar punctuations and nearly weightless brushes.
Saxophone and guitar reunite for a smaller, more spacious return of the motif, brightening briefly without becoming cheerful.

production: Tactile acoustic quartet recording in an intimate, dimly lit room; warm close-miked guitar and bass, mellow centered saxophone, softly rounded brushes, restrained dynamics, moderate stereo width, gentle room ambience, and a deliberately softened unresolved ending.
assumptions: Target BPM set near 82 to realize the requested medium-slow swing.
The supplied 150-second arc is divided into five flexible sections.
lyriaPrompt: Late-night noir jazz quartet for relaxation, 150 seconds, gentle medium-slow 4/4 swing around 82 BPM. Instrumental only, no vocals. Use warm hollow-body guitar, mellow breathy alto saxophone, round upright bass, and featherlight brush kit with softened ride. Begin quietly with guitar introducing a simple four-note motif; add discreet walking bass and brushed swing. Let alto saxophone reshape the motif in longer phrases while guitar answers with short figures rather than extended solos. Use lyrical major-minor interchange, secondary dominants, and occasional chromatic mediant turns that brighten briefly without becoming cheerful. Give upright bass a short foreground interlude, then return to a smaller guitar-and-sax statement. Keep spacious phrasing, restrained dynamics, tactile acoustic playing, intimate room ambience, and a softly unresolved ending. Avoid harsh brightness, heavy backbeat, flashy virtuosity, abrupt drops, cinematic bombast, and triumphant resolution.
